title: Durable Functions: orchestration, fan-out and long-running state

videos.script: An order at the shop is three steps. Reserve the stock, charge the customer, ship the parcel. {{flow}} Written as one function, the three steps live and die together. The function times out, or its instance goes away halfway. Then nobody knows which steps ran. Durable Functions keeps the steps in your code and the progress in storage. {{app}} You will add it to the function app of lesson 15. One function starts an order. An orchestrator says the steps, and activities do them. You will start an order over HTTP and watch its status go from Pending to Completed. {{replay}} Then a surprise. For one order, your orchestrator runs four times, and the log shows each run. Every run reads the history back from a table in Azurite. That is why an orchestrator must decide the same thing every time. {{fanout}} Next, an order with sixty lines, reserved all at once. You will find the limit that splits them into two waves. {{wait}} Last, waiting. A Pix payment that arrives, one that never does, and an order cancelled by hand. Nothing of yours runs while an order waits. The order survives a restart. A careless deployment is another matter.
